profile.behavior: Chiefly nocturnal and nonmigratory. Hunts from low perches by watching or listening for prey, then pouncing or making short flights; also takes insects and bats in flight. Roosts and nests in tree cavities or nest boxes and gives whinnying calls and soft trills.
field_marks: Short, stocky body with a large head and almost no visible neck
Pointed ear tufts that can be raised or flattened
Gray, brown, or rufous plumage with dark streaks, fine barring, and pale mottling
Small hooked bill; feathered legs and strong talons
Broad, rounded wings and a short, square-tipped tail
profile.habitat: Deciduous, mixed, or evergreen woodland with large cavity-bearing trees and some open understory; also wooded farmland, parks, and suburban landscapes, particularly near water. Avoids extensive treeless habitats.

findings: Species identity is correct: the plate depicts a compact, large-headed Eastern Screech-Owl with prominent ear tufts, yellow eyes, cryptic gray-brown plumage, dark streaking, fine barring, pale mottling, rounded wings, and a short square-ended tail. These features agree with the attached references and live Cornell, Audubon, and Smithsonian accounts.

The plate contains exactly one primary specimen with one head, one hooked bill, two visible eyes, one tail, two attached feathered legs, and two intact feet gripping the branch. The near-side folded wing is complete; the far-side wing is naturally occluded by the body with convincing attachment geometry.

The detached spread-wing and side-profile head are clearly intentional supplementary studies. The wing has coherent feather layering and a broad rounded outline. The profile study has a correctly directed, proportionate hooked bill without a reversed, truncated, or exaggerated mandible.
All visible identification text is spelled correctly: “Eastern Screech-Owl,” “Megascops asio,” and “Strigidae.”

All three printed measurements exactly match the proposed profile and Cornell’s published values: “Length: Both sexes: 16–25 cm (6.3–9.8 in),” “Wingspan: Both sexes: 48–61 cm (18.9–24.0 in),” and “Weight: Both sexes: 121–244 g (4.3–8.6 oz).”
The habitat and behavior paragraphs reproduce the proposed wording completely, without duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical words. Their substantive claims agree with the live sources.

Every field-mark line reproduces the proposed wording correctly. The claims about body shape, ear tufts, yellow eyes, gray/brown/rufous variation, streaking and barring, hooked bill, feathered legs, talons, rounded wings, and short square-tipped tail are supported by the direct sources.

The vertical body-length diagram is internally consistent: 16 cm (6.3 in) is the lower endpoint, 25 cm (9.8 in) is the upper endpoint, values increase upward, the adjacent range agrees, and “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” clearly prevents interpreting it as the printed specimen’s physical scale.
The palette labels are all legible and correctly spelled: “bark gray,” “rufous brown,” “dark brown,” “cream white,” and “golden yellow.”
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, locality, date, or other local-observation detail appears on the plate.
